slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: Serum HDL cholesterol is measured directly, without pre-treatment or centrifugation; the reaction has two steps.
Step 1 (R1): cholesterol of non-HDL lipoproteins is eliminated by CHE, CHOD and catalase (H2O2 is destroyed).
Step 2 (R2): HDL cholesterol, with CHE/CHOD/POD, HDAOS and 4-aminoantipyrine, gives a coloured quinone pigment; the colour is proportional to HDL-C.
Alternative methods exist (e.g. HDL precipitation) — they follow their own IFU and are not included here.

slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “HDLc-D” kit (IFU BSIS37-I, 13/09/18). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum, heparin or EDTA plasma; centrifuge if precipitates are present. Stable 6 days at 2–8 °C, 1 year at −70 °C.
R1: buffer pH 6.6, HDAOS 0.7 mM, CHE ≥ 800 U/L, CHOD ≥ 500 U/L, catalase ≥ 300 U/L, ascorbate oxidase ≥ 3000 U/L. R2: buffer pH 7.0, 4-aminoantipyrine, POD ≥ 3500 U/L.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Calibrator: lyophilised human serum (HDLc/LDLc CAL); its concentration is on the vial label.
Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 570 nm, 1.0 cm cuvettes, 37 °C thermostat.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: R1 and R2 are ready to use. Calibrator: dissolve the vial contents in 1 mL of distilled water, cap and mix gently.
Reconstituted calibrator: stable 30 hours at 20–25 °C, 2 weeks at 2–8 °C or 3 months at −20 °C.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: Store the reagents at 2–8 °C; do not freeze. The yellowish colour of R2 comes from the peroxidase and does not affect it.
Two-reagent method: enter R1 and R2 as separate steps in the analyser programme (A1 before R2, A2 after R2).

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The values come from the SPINREACT “HDLc-D” IFU (BSIS37-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 550–650 nm (the equipment section gives 570 nm); temperature 37 °C.
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: blank — R1 300 µL; calibrator — R1 300 µL + calibrator 3 µL; sample — R1 300 µL + sample 3 µL.
4. Mix, incubate for 5 minutes at 37 °C and read A1.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Add 100 µL of R2 to each cuvette.
6. Mix, incubate for 5 minutes at 37 °C and read A2 against the blank.

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: HDL-C programme
rows: R1 300 µL + sample 3 µL; R2 100 µL

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: HDL-C (mg/dL) = [(A2 − A1) sample − (A2 − A1) blank] / [(A2 − A1) calibrator − (A2 − A1) blank] × calibrator concentration.
Conversion: mg/dL × 0.0259 = mmol/L.
Measuring range 5.0 to 151 mg/dL; above that, dilute 1/2 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 2.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: Risk (IFU): men — low > 50, normal 35–50, high < 35 mg/dL; women — low > 60, normal 45–60, high < 45 mg/dL.
These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Bilirubin up to 30 mg/dL, haemoglobin up to 500 mg/dL, rheumatoid factor up to 1000 IU/mL and lipaemia up to 1200 mg/dL do not interfere.
If triglycerides are > 1200 mg/dL, dilute the sample 1/10 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 10.
The IFU gives the wavelength in two ways (550–650 nm and 570 nm) — 570 nm lies within that range; choose your analyser filter from your own IFU.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: IFU: performance depends on the analyser used.

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and calibrator; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: The calibrator is human serum: tested negative for HBsAg, HCV and antibody to HIV (1/2), but handle it as potentially infectious.
Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
